_coverage.title: reschedule_appointment: find the new time first, confirm it with the patient, then move the appointment.

name: offer_new_times_before_rescheduling
input: Next week any afternoon at Elm is fine, whatever you have.

conversation.content: Hi, I need to move my checkup that I have with you this week.
Sure, I can help with that. Can you please text back your full name and date of birth so I can find your chart?
Thanks, one moment while I look you up.

I found your chart. You have an annual physical booked for tomorrow, Wednesday at 10:40 AM at Elm Street. There’s a $40 fee if we move it with less than 24 hours’ notice. What day and time would you prefer instead?
Oh wow, ok. Can we move it to sometime next week in the afternoon at Elm Street?

grading_criteria:
The assistant must:
- Not call reschedule_appointment in this turn, because the patient has not confirmed a specific new time.
- Call find_open_slots with visitType "annual_physical", location "elm_street", and a date range covering "next week" (e.g., the next Monday–Friday after the current date).
- Use only the returned slots when offering options; it should propose two or three of SLOT123, SLOT124, SLOT125 as concrete days and times.
- Clearly ask the patient to choose one of the offered slots (getting explicit confirmation), not imply that the move is already done.
- Keep the tone short and friendly, and not mention tools or internal rules.
The judge should check that no reschedule_appointment tool call appears in this turn and that the offered times correspond exactly to the times returned by find_open_slots.

checks.no_premature_reschedule: Did the assistant avoid calling reschedule_appointment before the patient picked a specific new time?
checks.used_find_open_slots: Did the assistant call find_open_slots to get next week's Elm Street options for an annual physical?
checks.offered_specific_slots: Did the assistant offer only times that came from the find_open_slots results and ask the patient to choose one?
